sources.quote: "The stress pattern is similar to the normal Turkic one. The stressed syllable is normally the last syllable in the word. The realisation of the stress is, however, different from other Turkic languages, because stress and high-pitch falls always on the same syllable. When a suffix that cannot carry stress, as for instance the negation suffix -MA, the preceding syllable is stressed, e.g. anlamadym [ɑn'lɑmɑdïm] 'I didn't understand (it)'. Compounds are stressed on their first element, e.g. biugiu

sources.note: Read online: one prosody sentence only — stress is 'dynamic' (expiratory), attributed to Slavic influence, retracting before certain unstressable affixes (instrumental, person, negation); no mention of tone or pitch. The clause 'падает почти на любой слог' (falls on almost any syllable) is odd and probably a compression of 'final except before unstressable affixes'; treat as secondhand.

tone.quote: Ударение динамическое из-за влияния славянских языков, падает почти на любой слог, кроме некоторых словообразовательных аффиксов (инструментального, лица и отрицания) — в таких случаях ударение перемещается на предыдущий слог.
tone.locator: section 'Фонетика' of the online grammatical sketch (unpaginated HTML)
tone.translation: Stress is dynamic owing to the influence of the Slavic languages; it falls on almost any syllable except certain derivational affixes (instrumental, person and negation) — in such cases the stress moves to the preceding syllable.

tone.quote: Der Druck (Akzent) ist überall, wo er nicht auf der letzten Silbe ruht, durcheine kleine senkrechte Linie vor der betonten Silbe bezeichnet. Diese Linie bedeutet, wenn oben angebracht, den Hauptdruck, wenn unten angebracht den Nebendruck.
tone.locator: p. LXXIII ('durcheine' = 'durch eine' in print); compound/verb stress remarks pp. XXXII-XXXIII
tone.translation: Stress (accent), wherever it does not rest on the last syllable, is marked by a small vertical line before the stressed syllable. Placed above, this line means main stress; placed below, secondary stress.
